days.focus_note: Fasting builds spiritual power and blesses people in need; honoring the Lord on the Sabbath brings joy.
days.source_excerpt: Isaiah 58:3–12 — Fasting builds spiritual power and blesses people in need. Why would anyone voluntarily go without food when food is available? ... Why can fasting sometimes be perceived like more of a burden than a blessing? (see Isaiah 58:3–5). ... What might it mean to 'loose the bands of wickedness' and 'break every yoke'? (Isaiah 58:6). How can fasting bless others? (see verse 7). How has fasting brought you the blessings described in Isaiah 58:8–12? ... Isaiah 58:13–14 — Honoring the Lord on the Sabbath brings joy. Is the Sabbath day 'a delight' for you? ... what might it mean to turn 'from doing thy pleasure on [His] holy day'? What is the difference between '[delighting] thyself in the Lord' and 'doing thine own ways'?

days.focus_note: Jesus Christ is my Savior and Redeemer — the Intercessor who overcomes the conditions of sin described in this chapter.
days.source_excerpt: Isaiah 59:9–21; 61:1–3; 63:7–9 — Jesus Christ is my Savior and Redeemer. Isaiah 58–66 has multiple references to the atoning mission of Jesus Christ. ... What impresses you about the description of the 'intercessor' in Isaiah 59:16–21? How does the Savior overcome the conditions described in verses 9–15?

days.focus_note: 'The Lord shall be unto thee an everlasting light' — gospel light gathering God's children out of darkness.
days.source_excerpt: Isaiah 60; 62 — 'The Lord shall be unto thee an everlasting light.' Isaiah 60 and 62 speak of light and dark, eyes and seeing to teach about how the gospel of Jesus Christ will bless the world in the last days. Look for these concepts in Isaiah 60:1–5, 19–20; 62:1–2. ... 'Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee' (Isaiah 60:1).

days.focus_note: Christ's declaration in the synagogue at Nazareth fulfilling Isaiah 61; continuing the theme of light and Zion's restoration from Isaiah 62.
days.source_excerpt: When Jesus Christ announced to the people of Nazareth that He was the Messiah, He quoted from Isaiah 61:1–3 (see Luke 4:16–21). How has Jesus Christ blessed you and others in the ways described in these verses? How has He given beauty in place of ashes? ... Isaiah 60 and 62 speak of light and dark, eyes and seeing ... As you read these chapters, ponder how God is gathering His children out of darkness to His light. What is your role in this work?

days.focus_note: The 'lovingkindnesses of the Lord' and a plea for the Lord to come down, pointing toward His merciful intervention.
days.source_excerpt: What 'lovingkindnesses of the Lord' can you 'mention'? (see Isaiah 63:7–9). ... Isaiah 64:1–5; 65:17–25; 66 — Christ will reign on earth during the Millennium. Isaiah spoke of a day when 'the former troubles are forgotten' (Isaiah 65:16). ... Isaiah described this future day in Isaiah 64:1–5.

days.focus_note: Christ will reign on earth during the Millennium; new heavens and new earth; a day of rejoicing at the Savior's coming.
days.source_excerpt: Isaiah 65:17–25; 66 — While this prophecy has several fulfillments, in its fullest sense, that day is yet to come—when Jesus Christ will return. Isaiah described this future day in Isaiah 64:1–5; 65:17–25; 66. Notice how often he used words like 'rejoice' and 'rejoicing.' Why will the Savior's return be a day of rejoicing for you? What can you do to prepare for His coming? ... Isaiah 65:17–25 describes what the earth will be like when the Savior comes again. ... Why will this be a time to be 'glad and rejoice for ever'? (verse 18).
